modes.label: Year over year
modes.description: Each period against the observation closest to four quarters earlier. Like for like -- Q3 against Q3 -- so seasonality cancels.

modes.label: Quarter over quarter
modes.description: Each period against the one immediately before it. **Not seasonally adjusted**: a seasonal business shows a regular yearly cycle here that is the calendar, not the trend.

metrics.label: Revenue growth
metrics.description: How much larger trailing-twelve-month sales are than a year ago. The top line, and the number hardest to influence through accounting choices.
metrics.formula: calculate_growth on `Revenue_TTM`, 4-quarter lag. `Revenue` is mapped per profile -- for `financial` it is RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense, not gross revenue.

metrics.label: Income growth
metrics.description: The same year-over-year comparison applied to profit after everything.
metrics.formula: calculate_growth on `NetIncomeLoss_TTM`, 4-quarter lag.

metrics.label: Operating Margin
metrics.description: Cents of operating profit per dollar of sales, before interest and tax.
metrics.formula: `OperatingIncomeLoss_TTM` / `Revenue_TTM`. A self-relative scale guard blanks periods where Revenue_TTM falls below 10% of its own max over the surrounding ±8 quarters, which suppresses ratios built on a partially-filed quarter.

metrics.label: Return on Equity
metrics.description: Profit earned per dollar of shareholders' equity.
metrics.formula: `NetIncomeLoss_TTM` / `StockholdersEquity`. Equity is the point-in-time balance, NOT a period average. Requires positive equity, and equity of at least 1% of Revenue_TTM.

metrics.label: Debt-to-Equity Ratio
metrics.description: Long-term borrowings measured against the equity cushion beneath them.
metrics.formula: `LongTermDebt` / `StockholdersEquity`, both point-in-time. Long-term debt only -- short-term borrowings are not included. Requires positive equity of at least 5% of LongTermDebt.

metrics.label: Payout Ratio
metrics.description: The share of earnings paid out as dividends.
metrics.formula: `DividendsPerShare_TTM` / `EPS_TTM_CALC`, requires a positive denominator. EPS_TTM_CALC is the pipeline's own figure (see P/E), not reported EPS.

metrics.label: Free Cash Flow Margin
metrics.description: Cents of free cash flow per dollar of sales -- how much of the revenue actually becomes spendable cash.
metrics.formula: (`OperatingCashFlow_TTM` − `Capex_TTM`) / `Revenue_TTM`, with the same ±8-quarter self-relative revenue guard as the operating margin.

metrics.label: Net Debt / EBITDA
metrics.description: Years of current earnings it would take to repay borrowings net of cash.
metrics.formula: (`LongTermDebt` − `CashAndEquivalents`) / (`OperatingIncomeLoss_TTM` + `DepreciationAndAmortization_TTM`). Blanked when |EBITDA| < $10m or the result exceeds ±60.

metrics.label: Rule of 40
metrics.description: Growth plus cash-flow margin, the software-industry trade-off between growing and being profitable. Above 40% is the convention.
metrics.formula: `revenue_yoy_growth` + `fcf_margin`, both as fractions -- so the 0.4 reference line is the conventional 40%. Inherits the TTM basis of both.

metrics.label: Net Interest Margin
metrics.description: A bank's spread: interest earned minus interest paid, per dollar of assets.
metrics.formula: `NetInterestIncome_TTM` / `Assets`. Denominator is TOTAL assets at period end, not average earning assets, so the level runs below the conventional NIM.

metrics.label: Efficiency Ratio
metrics.description: What a bank spends to earn a dollar of revenue. Lower is better; this is the one ratio where a falling line is the good news.
metrics.formula: `NoninterestExpense_TTM` / `Revenue_TTM`. For the `financial` profile Revenue maps to RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense, which makes this close to the conventional bank efficiency ratio.

metrics.label: Return on Assets
metrics.description: Profit per dollar of assets, the return measure that ignores leverage.
metrics.formula: `NetIncomeLoss_TTM` / `Assets`, assets point-in-time rather than averaged.

metrics.label: Equity / Assets
metrics.description: The simple capital ratio: what fraction of the balance sheet is shareholders' money rather than borrowed.
metrics.formula: `StockholdersEquity` / `Assets`, both point-in-time. Book equity, not a regulatory capital measure such as CET1.

metrics.label: Provision/Revenue
metrics.description: How much of revenue is being set aside against expected credit losses.
metrics.formula: `ProvisionForCreditLosses_TTM` / `Revenue_TTM`. Denominator is revenue, not average loans, so this is not the conventional provisioning rate.

metrics.label: Combined Ratio
metrics.description: An insurer's claims and expenses per dollar of premium. Above 100% means underwriting loses money, and the investment income has to make up for it.
metrics.formula: `BenefitsLossesAndExpenses_TTM` / `EarnedPremiums_TTM` -- a single reported aggregate over premiums, not losses and expenses summed separately.

metrics.label: Loss Ratio
metrics.description: The claims half of the combined ratio: payouts per dollar of premium.
metrics.formula: `IncurredLosses_TTM` / `EarnedPremiums_TTM`.

metrics.label: Expense Ratio
metrics.description: The cost half of the combined ratio: what it costs to write the business.
metrics.formula: `combined_ratio` − `loss_ratio`, so TTM like both of them. Obtained by subtraction, not from a reported expense figure, so it absorbs any difference in how the two source tags are drawn.

metrics.label: Net Investment Yield
metrics.description: What an insurer earns on the float it holds between premium and claim.
metrics.formula: `NetInvestmentIncome_TTM` / `Investments`, investments point-in-time.

metrics.label: Reserve Growth
metrics.description: Year-over-year change in the reserve set aside for future claims.
metrics.formula: calculate_growth on `ClaimsReserve`, 4-quarter lag, point-in-time balance.

metrics.label: Inventory Turnover (x/Year)
metrics.description: How many times a year the shelves are emptied and refilled.
metrics.formula: `CostOfRevenue_TTM` / `Inventory`. Period-end inventory, not the average balance the textbook ratio uses.

metrics.label: Days Inventory Outstanding
metrics.description: Days of stock on hand at the current rate of sale.
metrics.formula: `Inventory` / `CostOfRevenue_TTM` × 365, period-end inventory.

metrics.label: Days Sales Outstanding
metrics.description: Days between making a sale and being paid for it.
metrics.formula: `AccountsReceivable` / `Revenue_TTM` × 365, period-end receivables.

metrics.label: Days Payable Outstanding
metrics.description: Days the company takes to pay its own suppliers.
metrics.formula: `AccountsPayable` / `CostOfRevenue_TTM` × 365, period-end payables.

metrics.label: Cash Conversion Cycle (Days)
metrics.description: Days of cash tied up in working capital. Negative means suppliers finance the business -- customers pay before the bills come due.
metrics.formula: `dio` + `dso` − `dpo`; inherits the period-end balances of all three.

metrics.label: R&D Intensity (% Revenue)
metrics.description: The share of revenue reinvested into research and development.
metrics.formula: `ResearchAndDevelopment_TTM` / `Revenue_TTM`.

metrics.label: CapEx Intensity (% Revenue)
metrics.description: The share of revenue spent on property, plant and equipment.
metrics.formula: `Capex_TTM` / `Revenue_TTM`.

metrics.label: Operating Leverage
metrics.description: How much faster operating profit moves than sales. Above 1 means growth is amplified on the way down as well as up.
metrics.formula: `operating_income_yoy_growth` / `revenue_yoy_growth`, both TTM growth rates. Blanked when revenue growth is under ±2% (a near-zero denominator) or the result exceeds ±15.

metrics.label: Operating Income YOY Growth
metrics.description: Year-over-year change in operating profit.
metrics.formula: calculate_growth on `OperatingIncomeLoss_TTM`, 4-quarter lag.

metrics.label: FFO Margin (% Revenue)
metrics.description: Funds from operations per dollar of revenue -- the REIT profitability measure, since depreciation makes reported net income misleading for property.
metrics.formula: `FFO_TTM` / `Revenue_TTM`, where FFO_TTM = `NetIncomeLoss_TTM` + `DepreciationAndAmortization_TTM` − `GainLossOnSaleOfProperties_TTM`. Total D&A is added back, not only real-estate depreciation as NAREIT specifies.

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.description: Price per dollar of annual earnings -- the years of current profit you are paying for one share.
metrics.formula: close / `EPS_TTM_CALC`, where EPS_TTM_CALC = `NetIncomeLoss_TTM` / `SharesOutstanding`. Computed, not the reported diluted EPS, and the share count is normally the diluted weighted average. Only positive EPS is plotted.

metrics.label: P/B
metrics.description: Market value per dollar of book equity.
metrics.formula: market cap / `StockholdersEquity`, equity point-in-time at the period end, positive only. Additionally blanked when TangibleEquity is negative, since book value carried by goodwill is not a meaningful denominator.

metrics.label: P/FCF (TTM)
metrics.description: Price per dollar of free cash flow -- the earnings equivalent that is harder to manipulate.
metrics.formula: market cap / `FCF_TTM`, where FCF_TTM = `OperatingCashFlow_TTM` − `Capex_TTM`. Positive FCF only.

metrics.label: EV/FCF (TTM)
metrics.description: The same, but priced as if you bought the whole company including its debt.
metrics.formula: EV / `FCF_TTM`, EV = market cap + `LongTermDebt` − `CashAndEquivalents`. Short-term debt, minority interest and preferred are not in this EV.

metrics.label: P/FCF ex-SBC (TTM)
metrics.description: P/FCF after treating stock-based compensation as the real cost it is. The gap against plain P/FCF is how much of the cash flow is paid for in shares.
metrics.formula: market cap / (`FCF_TTM` − `ShareBasedCompensation_TTM`).

metrics.label: EV/EBITDA
metrics.description: Enterprise value per dollar of pre-depreciation operating profit; the standard cross-company multiple because it is indifferent to capital structure.
metrics.formula: EV / `EBITDA_TTM`, EBITDA_TTM = `OperatingIncomeLoss_TTM` + `DepreciationAndAmortization_TTM` (built up from operating income, not from net income).

metrics.label: EV/Sales
metrics.description: Enterprise value per dollar of revenue -- the fallback multiple when a company has no profit to divide by.
metrics.formula: EV / `Revenue_TTM`.

metrics.label: dividend yield
metrics.description: Cash dividends over the last year as a percentage of the share price.
metrics.formula: `DividendsPerShare_TTM` / close. Dividends declared per share; buybacks are not included.

metrics.label: P/TBV
metrics.description: Price per dollar of book value with goodwill stripped out -- the standard bank and insurer multiple, because acquired goodwill absorbs losses first.
metrics.formula: market cap / (`StockholdersEquity` − `Goodwill`), both point-in-time at the period end. Only goodwill is removed; other intangibles stay in, so this sits above a strict tangible book value.

metrics.label: P/PPNR
metrics.description: Price against a bank's earnings power before credit losses -- what it earns in a normal year, independent of where it is in the credit cycle.
metrics.formula: market cap / `PPNR`, PPNR = `NetInterestIncome_TTM` + `NoninterestIncome_TTM` − `NoninterestExpense_TTM`.

metrics.label: P/Core Earnings
metrics.description: Price against insurance earnings with investment gains removed, since realised gains are a timing choice rather than underwriting performance.
metrics.formula: market cap / `CoreOperatingEarnings`, = `NetIncomeLoss_TTM` − `RealizedInvestmentGains_TTM`. A subtraction of realised gains only.

metrics.label: P/FFO (TTM)
metrics.description: The REIT equivalent of P/E, using funds from operations because property depreciation is an accounting charge rather than an economic one.
metrics.formula: market cap / `FFO_TTM` (see FFO Margin for the FFO build-up).

metrics.label: PE to Revenue Growth
metrics.description: A PEG-style ratio: the P/E divided by the growth rate that justifies it. Below 1 is the conventional 'growth is cheap' threshold.
metrics.formula: `pe_ratio` / (revenue growth in percentage points). Uses REVENUE growth, not earnings growth as a textbook PEG does. That growth rate is also its own figure -- Revenue_TTM.pct_change(4) computed inside build_valuation_history, not the guarded calculate_growth used elsewhere. Requires growth above 2%; results beyond ±30 are dropped.

metrics.label: Revenue growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Sales in this quarter against the earlier quarter the chart's mode selects -- four quarters back, or the one immediately before.
metrics.formula: Single quarter as filed. The lag is the mode's, not this metric's; see the growth mechanism note.

metrics.label: Net Income Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Quarterly profit against the earlier quarter the mode selects. Gappy by design: a loss quarter on either side produces no value at all.
metrics.formula: Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Shares Outstanding (Stock Dilution/Repurchase)
metrics.description: Change in the share count -- negative means buybacks, positive means dilution. Every per-share figure moves with this line.
metrics.formula: Point-in-time share count, normally the diluted weighted average, restated onto the current split basis by parse_edgar._apply_split_basis -- which applies only splits the corporate-action feed reports and the filer's own restatements confirm, so an uncorroborated period is left as filed.

metrics.label: EPS Growth (TTM)
metrics.description: Growth in earnings per share on a trailing-twelve-month basis -- profit growth and share-count change combined into the number that reaches the shareholder.
metrics.formula: `NetIncomeLoss_TTM` / `SharesOutstanding`, the pipeline's own EPS.

metrics.label: Free Cash Flow Growth (TTM)
metrics.description: Growth in trailing free cash flow.
metrics.formula: `OperatingCashFlow_TTM` − `Capex_TTM`.

metrics.label: Operating Income Growth (TTM)
metrics.description: Growth in trailing operating profit, before interest and tax.
metrics.formula: `OperatingIncomeLoss_TTM`. Hidden for `financial`: banks do not file an operating-income line, so the panel would always be empty.

metrics.label: Equity Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in book equity -- retained profit less dividends and buybacks. The compounding measure for a bank or insurer.
metrics.formula: Point-in-time `StockholdersEquity`.

metrics.label: PPNR Growth (TTM)
metrics.description: Growth in a bank's pre-provision earnings power.
metrics.formula: `NetInterestIncome_TTM` + `NoninterestIncome_TTM` − `NoninterestExpense_TTM`.

metrics.label: Core Operating Earnings Growth (TTM)
metrics.description: Growth in insurance earnings excluding realised investment gains.
metrics.formula: `NetIncomeLoss_TTM` − `RealizedInvestmentGains_TTM`.

metrics.label: FFO Growth (TTM)
metrics.description: Growth in a REIT's funds from operations.
metrics.formula: `NetIncomeLoss_TTM` + `DepreciationAndAmortization_TTM` − `GainLossOnSaleOfProperties_TTM`.

metrics.label: Cost of Revenue Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in the direct cost of what was sold. Read next to `Revenue` growth: cost rising faster than sales is margin compression in its rawest form.
metrics.formula: `CostOfRevenue`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Operating Income Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in quarterly operating profit, before interest and tax. The quarterly counterpart of the TTM panel, and the more volatile of the two.
metrics.formula: `OperatingIncomeLoss`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Pre-tax Income Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in profit before tax -- operating profit plus financing and other items, with the tax line still to come.
metrics.formula: `PretaxIncome`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Income Tax Expense Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in the tax charge. Moves with pre-tax income unless the effective rate changed; a divergence between the two is what `effective_tax_rate` measures.
metrics.formula: `IncomeTaxExpense`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Operating Cash Flow Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in cash generated by operations, before capital spending.
metrics.formula: `OperatingCashFlow`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Capital Expenditure Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in capital spending. Lumpy by nature -- a single plant or acquisition of equipment moves one quarter and not its neighbours.
metrics.formula: `Capex`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: D&A Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in depreciation and amortisation. Follows past capital spending and acquisition accounting rather than current activity.
metrics.formula: `DepreciationAndAmortization`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: R&D Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in research and development spending.
metrics.formula: `ResearchAndDevelopment`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Share-based Compensation Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in the stock-compensation charge. The cash-flow-statement add-back that `pfcf_ex_sbc` subtracts again.
metrics.formula: `ShareBasedCompensation`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Dividend per Share Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in the dividend declared per share. Only filers that declare one produce a value; the rest have an empty panel, which is a fact about the company.
metrics.formula: `DividendsPerShare`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Stock Issued Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in the value of stock issued in the quarter. One input to `share_count_jump_flag`.
metrics.formula: `StockIssued`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Stock Repurchased Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in the value of stock bought back in the quarter. The cash side of what `SharesOutstanding` shows as a count.
metrics.formula: `StockRepurchased`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Total Assets Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in the balance-sheet total. For a bank this is the balance sheet itself; for an operating company it is mostly a lagging indicator of investment.
metrics.formula: `Assets`, the filed EDGAR fact. Point-in-time balance as filed.

metrics.label: Cash Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in cash and equivalents. Swings with financing and working capital rather than with trading, so a large move is a question rather than an answer.
metrics.formula: `CashAndEquivalents`, the filed EDGAR fact. Point-in-time balance as filed.

metrics.label: Goodwill Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in goodwill. Rises on acquisitions and falls on impairment, so it is the clearest balance-sheet trace of inorganic activity -- the same signal `inorganic_contaminated` flags.
metrics.formula: `Goodwill`, the filed EDGAR fact. Point-in-time balance as filed.

metrics.label: Inventory Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in inventory. Rising faster than revenue is the classic build-up signal; `inventory_turnover` and `dio` measure the same thing as a ratio.
metrics.formula: `Inventory`, the filed EDGAR fact. Point-in-time balance as filed.

metrics.label: Receivables Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in trade receivables. Outrunning revenue growth means sales are being collected more slowly, which `dso` states in days.
metrics.formula: `AccountsReceivable`, the filed EDGAR fact. Point-in-time balance as filed.

metrics.label: Payables Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in trade payables -- what the company owes suppliers. `dpo` states the same thing in days.
metrics.formula: `AccountsPayable`, the filed EDGAR fact. Point-in-time balance as filed.

metrics.label: Long-term Debt Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in long-term borrowings. The denominator side of leverage; `net_debt_to_ebitda` pairs it with earnings.
metrics.formula: `LongTermDebt`, the filed EDGAR fact. Point-in-time balance as filed.

metrics.label: Net Interest Income Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: A bank's core revenue line: interest earned less interest paid. `net_interest_margin` is the same quantity against earning assets.
metrics.formula: `NetInterestIncome`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Noninterest Income Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: A bank's fee and trading income -- everything that is not net interest income.
metrics.formula: `NoninterestIncome`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Noninterest Expense Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: A bank's operating cost base. `efficiency_ratio` measures it against revenue.
metrics.formula: `NoninterestExpense`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Credit Loss Provision Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in the charge a bank takes for expected loan losses. Rises ahead of a credit cycle rather than during it.
metrics.formula: `ProvisionForCreditLosses`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Earned Premiums Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in an insurer's earned premium -- its top line.
metrics.formula: `EarnedPremiums`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Incurred Losses Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in claims incurred. Against `EarnedPremiums` growth this is the `loss_ratio` moving.
metrics.formula: `IncurredLosses`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Benefits, Losses and Expenses Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in a life insurer's total benefit and expense line.
metrics.formula: `BenefitsLossesAndExpenses`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Net Investment Income Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in the return an insurer earns on its investment portfolio. `net_investment_yield` is the same quantity against the portfolio.
metrics.formula: `NetInvestmentIncome`, the filed EDGAR fact. Single quarter as filed.

metrics.label: Investment Portfolio Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in an insurer's invested assets.
metrics.formula: `Investments`, the filed EDGAR fact. Point-in-time balance as filed.

metrics.label: Claims Reserve Growth (Quartal)
metrics.description: Growth in the reserve held against unpaid claims. `reserve_growth` is the fundamentals-chart version of the same series.
metrics.formula: `ClaimsReserve`, the filed EDGAR fact. Point-in-time balance as filed.

notes.growth_mechanism:
Every growth panel is produced by the same function, with certain guards applied in order to exclude absurd values.

- **Two lags, one computation.** The chart's mode control switches which of two
  columns is drawn. **YoY** compares each period against the observation closest
  to 365 days earlier (tolerance ±45 days), so a quarterly series is compared
  like for like -- Q3 against Q3 -- and seasonality cancels. **QoQ** compares it
  against the one closest to 91 days earlier (tolerance ±11 days). Both are
  `calculate_growth` with a different `periods` argument and are subject to
  every guard below identically; nothing else differs.
- **QoQ is not seasonally adjusted.** This is the one thing to know before
  reading it. A seasonal filer shows a regular yearly cycle in QoQ that is the
  calendar rather than the business: measured across this universe, the spread
  between a panel's best and worst calendar quarter is a median 13.3 pp in QoQ
  against 8.9 pp in YoY, and 24 pp against 6 pp for retailers specifically.
  DECK's quarterly revenue growth runs -52%, -25%, +116%, +63% around the year
  while its YoY growth never leaves +8% to +13%. Both are correct; only one of
  them is about the business.
- **QoQ is not the noisier series, despite that.** A quarter-to-quarter change
  is measured over a shorter interval, so it is smaller: the median panel's QoQ
  standard deviation is **0.58x** its YoY one, and QoQ is the more volatile of
  the two on only 22.5% of panels. The sawtooth above is a *pattern*, not extra
  variance.
- **Annual-cadence series have no QoQ at all.** A filer publishing an item once
  a year leaves no observation inside the 91 ± 11 day window, so those panels
  are blank in QoQ and populated in YoY. 94 of 11,837 series in this export
  (0.8%). That is the absence of a preceding quarter, not a dropped value.
- **Both values must be positive.** If either the current or the prior figure is
  zero or negative, no growth value is produced. A percentage change across zero
  has no meaning, so the pipeline declines to invent one. This is why loss-making
  quarters leave holes in the net-income and cash-flow panels.
- **The minimum-base guard is off.** `calculate_growth` still takes a
  `min_base_ratio`, and it is now **0** everywhere -- the function default and all
  seven per-concept overrides. That parameter is a growth cap in disguise:
  requiring the prior value to be at least *r* times the current one is exactly
  capping growth at *1/r − 1*, so the old default of 0.33 capped every series at
  **+203%** and the 0.05 overrides (Capex, Goodwill, CashAndEquivalents,
  Inventory, LongTermDebt, ProvisionForCreditLosses, TangibleEquity) capped
  theirs at **+1,900%**. With it at 0, growth from a tiny but positive base is
  reported as computed. Measured on the current universe, that admits 33,070
  values (3.6% of the total) that were previously blank -- every one of them above
  +200% by construction, a quarter above +1,000%, and 282 above +100,000%. **A
  panel with one enormous spike and a flat remainder is that base, not the
  business**; the y-axis is shared across the panel, so a single such point
  flattens everything else in it. The same census on the QoQ column is slightly
  *smaller*, not larger: 3.1% of drawn values above +200% against YoY's 4.2%,
  and 19.6% of panels carry a point above +1,000% against YoY's 23.1%. The
  blow-ups come from a near-zero base either way, and a near-zero quarter's
  immediate neighbour is more often near-zero too.
- **A panel for every raw fact.** The catalogue is every concept the pipeline asks
  EDGAR for -- `get_concept_candidates`' keys -- rather than a curated ten, plus
  six derived series (`EPS_TTM_CALC`, `FCF_TTM`, `OperatingIncomeLoss_TTM`, `PPNR`,
  `CoreOperatingEarnings`, `FFO_TTM`) that have no raw counterpart. The `_TTM` and
  `_QUARTERLY` derivations of a raw fact are not registered: they are the same
  quantity on a different window, and the window is what this chart already varies.
  Sector-specific tags are offered to every profile, so a retailer sees bank and
  insurer panels drawing **No Data** -- that is the catalogue being universal, not
  a missing value.
- **TTM versus quarterly.** Panels labelled *TTM* run on a rolling four-quarter
  sum; those labelled *Quartal* run on the single quarter as filed. Measured
  across this ticker set, a quarterly growth series is roughly 1.1--2.2x more
  volatile than the TTM series of the same concept.
- **Annual-cadence series.** Some filers disclose an item only once a year --
  share-based compensation and pre-tax income are the common cases. There is then
  nothing quarterly to sum, so the pipeline reads the 12-month fact as filed
  instead, and the series carries one point per year. Its growth panel therefore
  shows one value per year too. **That is complete coverage of what the filer
  published, not missing data**, and it is the distinction the marked columns in
  the data tab exist to make: a column marked *annual cadence* is sparse by the
  filer's choice, an unmarked sparse column is a gap. Which path produced each
  value is recorded per row in the facts frame's `ttm_source` column
  (`quarterly_rolling` / `annual_fact`); the two are disjoint by construction, so
  no series mixes them.
- Two concepts are excluded from growth entirely -- GainLossOnSaleOfProperties
  and RealizedInvestmentGains -- because their level swings sign freely.
notes.valuation_mechanism:
All valuation multiples share one price convention and one averaging convention.

- **Which price.** Each period end is matched to the most recent daily close at
  or before it (a backward as-of join on the yfinance history), so the multiple
  is what the market was charging on the day the period closed -- not today's
  price applied to an old balance sheet.
- **Market cap and enterprise value.** Market cap is that close times the share
  count from EDGAR, falling back to yfinance where EDGAR reports none.
  EV = market cap + LongTermDebt − CashAndEquivalents. Short-term debt, minority
  interest and preferred stock are *not* in this enterprise value.
- **The mean line.** Multiples that compound multiplicatively use a **harmonic**
  mean, which is the correct average for a ratio and is not dragged upward by a
  few expensive quarters; the rest use an arithmetic mean. The harmonic set is
  read from the registry, not hardcoded. Only positive observations enter either.
- **The green marker** is the current value: today's price against the latest
  available fundamentals. It is a separate trace, deliberately excluded from the
  mean line so the historical benchmark is not contaminated by the value being
  judged against it, and it is hidden when an as-of date earlier than the
  snapshot is selected.
- **A scale guard** blanks any multiple whose denominator falls below 0.1% of
  Revenue_TTM, which removes the ratios that explode on a near-zero denominator.
